article.content: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. As domestic football returns to the pitch, the latest round of fixtures brings a series of pressing tactical questions and young talents stepping into the spotlight. According to Sport | The Guardian, the upcoming weekend action is set to test several struggling squads and highlight emerging prospects across the top flight. 

## Rising Talents and Defensive Redemptions

The report states that young prospect **Max Dowman** could potentially secure an opportunity to feature. Meanwhile, the spotlight turns heavily toward Stamford Bridge where Tottenham Hotspur are under pressure to establish tactical equilibrium, according to the publication. Defenders are also feeling the heat; the coverage indicates that **Axel Disasi** faces a firm requirement to make amends following previous performances. 

Beyond individual squad pressures, broader league dynamics continue to captivate supporters and analysts alike. As clubs navigate the demanding autumn fixture schedule, matches like these often serve as early indicators of which squads can sustain momentum and which will struggle to find their footing. Such tactical battles reflect the relentless competitive nature of the division, mirroring the broader financial and sporting dominance seen in recent international fixtures, such as those discussed in our coverage of a [dream night for Bournemouth - win over Milan a sign of Premier League power](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/dream-night-for-bournemouth-win-over-milan-a-sign-of-premier-league).

## Familiar Struggles for Nottingham Forest

The publication notes an uncanny parallel regarding **Nottingham Forest** after seven matches played. According to the article, their record mirrors last campaign almost identically, sitting at **five points** and **five goals scored**, mirroring their exact standing from a year prior. 

This statistical stagnation matters immensely for managers and supporters because early-season trends frequently dictate a club's entire trajectory. When teams fail to convert underlying performances into points, the psychological burden on the dressing room increases exponentially, often forcing hurried tactical shifts or premature pressure on coaching staff. 

Observers should monitor how managers address these recurring structural issues in upcoming team selections and whether under-pressure players like Disasi manage to retain their places in the starting lineup. 

Sources: [Sport | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/premier-league-10-things-to-look-out-for-this-weekend)
